searchText: bumping this: https://github.com/ethereum/eth1.0-specs/pull/221 <@!301186049323958275> question re: the 7 wei minimum what is the "math quirk" that makes that the effective minimum? 8 is the first number which multiplied by 1.125 gives a greater integer and if we round up starting at .5, then 5*1.125 would work too because it's 5.625 `7/8 == 0`, so if the parent base fee is 7 and the block is empty, we'll get a base fee delta of 7/8 which means we get a delta of 0. So we calculate the _delta_ and not the "newBaseFee", right? And `8 - 1/8 == 7`, so we can walk down to 7 but not further. We calculate the delta and then subtract that from the parent base fee. ``` newBaseFee = parentBaseFee - parentBaseFee * (parentGasTarget - parentGasUsed) // parentGasTarget // 8 ``` Where `//` rounds down for positive values. Got it. Thanks 🙂 On a related note... can I get multiple eyes on this change? It should be non-normative: https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/pull/3640 It has come to my attention that this unnecessary max has caused some confusion in implementations, and since it is a no-op we should remove it from the spec. Please triple check my work and verify it is actually a no-op!
